findings.claim: The how-to's Step 2 tells a repository on the immutable subject to pass its second identity's client ID and audience in Step 4, but the Step 4 snippet does not show those inputs. A reader who copies the snippet gets a 403 at the token exchange.

The how-to's Prerequisites bullets carry no links. .claude/rules/how-to-skeleton.md asks for each one to link to where the reader gets it, for example the localstack login session and the Tailscale admin console.

`jq -r .value` prints the string null when the OIDC response has no value field. The script then masks the word null in the whole log and posts null to Vault, which hides the real cause behind a Vault refusal. `jq -er '.value // empty'` would fail at the right step.

verdict.text: The change does what the plan says, and I found no defect that would ship.
The action passes inputs only through env, masks the JWT and the Vault token before anything writes them out, and fails when no token comes back.
The Vault role has the same shape as spike 2's working role.
The tailscale pin is v4, and the guard tests assert their rows.
What is left is two small gaps in the how-to and one hardening note, none of which needs another look from me.
`loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree: every gate passed (pre_commit, cli_tests, rows r1 to r5).
Stamp green `81dfe0a13ad615f7e75d8d759a1d57bec030a6a04ce92eb608a29eb9df79dd03`.
Pin: `gh api repos/tailscale/github-action/git/matching-refs/tags/v4` shows `refs/tags/v4` and `v4.4.0` both at `064b10558093f38325e838ddea35486bdc6b1d5c`.
At that SHA its action.yml has the inputs `oauth-client-id`, `audience`, `tags` and `args` (default empty).
Action security: no `${{ }}` in the run script, and vault-addr, vault-mount and vault-role come in through env.
The OIDC request is `$ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL&audience=vault.io` with the bearer request token, and a guard fails early when id-token permission is missing.
The JWT is masked right after it is fetched.
The Vault error path prints only Vault's error body.
`jq -e` with `// empty` fails when no client_token comes back.
The token is masked before the GITHUB_ENV and GITHUB_OUTPUT writes.
Vault role against spike 2 (`files/vault_bind.sh`, stdout): it has the same discovery URL and bound_issuer, `role_type` jwt, `user_claim` repository, `bound_claims_type` string, and the four claims.
workflow_ref is built as `<repo>/.github/workflows/<file>@<ref>`, the format spike 2 recorded.
The audience is vault.io, the TTL is 300 s and the max TTL 600 s.
r1: the test renders the role body through `terraform console` and asserts exact bound_claims, the audience, string type and a TTL under 3600 s.
It also refuses any other role on the mount.
r2: it finds every workflow job that uses the action and asserts no pull_request or pull_request_target trigger, plus environment, timeout-minutes and id-token write.
r3: it refuses secret, key, token or password input names and any `secrets.` reference.

The `with:` keys must be exactly oauth-client-id, audience and tags, args must be empty, `--accept-routes` must not appear, the audience must be only vault.io, and the mask must come before every export.
r4: exact default list.
Each test fails on its row's fails_when.
The eval's wording "oauth-client-id, audience" names the tailscale action's inputs, which the test pins; the lab-auth inputs are tailscale-client-id and tailscale-audience, as the plan says.
These agree.
lab-auth-check: treating a refused connection as FAIL is right.
The tailnet filter drops packets silently, so a RST means the packet passed the policy and reached a host.
A connection that cannot be made at all also counts as FAIL, which errs on the safe side.
The reach checks need a TLS answer (curl code 000 fails), so they also check the certificate.
r6: cannot be shown yet.
It needs the operator to apply and push, then a dispatch on main and a refused dispatch from a branch.
r7 (judged): the only identifiers committed are the federated client ID and audience, which are useless without a GitHub-signed token matching the subject.
No secrets input, and claude-ollama.yaml has no actions:write, so it cannot dispatch lab-auth-check.

r8 (judged): ADR 0027, the subnet-router page (its policy copy matches the handoff's description: tagOwners, both grants, the default ssh rule, the tests block), vault-identity (the mount, the bindings, the TTLs, MFA on the userpass accessor only, confirmed in identity.tf:121), the how-to (four sections, numbered steps, the immutable-subject step with a real API check; `use_immutable_subject` exists in the response, checked against this repo) and the reference inputs table match action.yml.
Apart from f1 and f2, these pages agree with the code.
Terraform layout: no new .tf file.
The mount and roles are in machine_roles.tf and the variable in variables.tf.
f1 (docs, non-blocking): Step 4's snippet should show the `tailscale-client-id` and `tailscale-audience` overrides for an immutable-subject repository, or Step 2 should give the snippet line.
f2 (docs, non-blocking): link each prerequisite, per the how-to skeleton rule.
f3 (hardening, non-blocking): make the JWT extraction fail on a missing value instead of passing the string null along.
The summary.md rewording outside the new bullet keeps it near the 500-word limit, and log.md records it.
